headline: DTEK says 3 of its 5 thermal plants knocked offline
dek: Russian officials said Ukraine set fire to a major oil refinery in Yaroslavl in an overnight drone attack. DTEK, Ukraine's largest private energy generator, said three of its five thermal power plants had been knocked offline, forcing outages in Kyiv and at least six other regions.
sources: Reuters, reporting Russian officials, DTEK, President Zelenskiy, and PM Sergii Koretskyi
fault_line: Energy war as election signal -- did Moscow time the barrage for the US vote, or is that Kyiv's framing of a winter campaign?

sections.what_happened: Russian officials said Ukraine set fire to a major oil refinery in Yaroslavl in an overnight drone attack. DTEK, Ukraine's largest private energy generator, said three of its five thermal power plants had been knocked offline, forcing outages in Kyiv and at least six other regions. PM Koretskyi said railways were hit (passenger carriages, locomotives, a station damaged). Zelenskiy: 'It is very telling that all of this is happening on the day of the US congressional elections... The Russians believe that America will not notice this signal.' The barrage itself (289 drones, 17 ballistic, 59 cruise missiles) was already recorded at 1500-01; this item adds only the Yaroslavl/DTEK/railway/Zelenskiy-timing elements, none of which appeared in the earlier record (grep-verified).
sections.what_verified: 1 declared family (Reuters); the companion Reuters piece the same day carries the same barrage numbers
sections.what_disputed: Russia's Defence Ministry frames its strikes as hitting electricity facilities supplying military factories and the army (same piece); no independent verification of the Yaroslavl damage extent is offered in the piece.
sections.why_matters: Monitor only, as an update to 1500-01: the overnight barrage's new numbers are 3-of-5 DTEK plants offline and a refinery fire at Yaroslavl -- no new strike event, no Short until the Yaroslavl damage is independently confirmed or the outage toll moves.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Reuters article crawled 12:05 UTC = 16:05 , pre-window, absent from the 1700 and 1800 items; updates 1500-01) -- Ukraine hits Yaroslavl refinery; DTEK says 3 of its 5 thermal plants knocked offline; Zelenskiy says Russian barrage 'timed for US vote'

totw_analysis: Our read: Monitor only, as an update to 1500-01: the overnight barrage's new numbers are 3-of-5 DTEK plants offline and a refinery fire at Yaroslavl -- no new strike event, no Short until the Yaroslavl damage is independently confirmed or the outage toll moves. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Energy war as election signal -- did Moscow time the barrage for the US vote, or is that Kyiv's framing of a winter campaign?
